prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type (sloped shingle vs. flat/membrane), budget, and whether you need insurance-claim experience. Instead of one name, I’ll give you what to look for and how to find and verify top hurricane-rated roof contractors in Miami. If you want, share your ZIP code and I’ll pull a short list of well-reviewed local contractors to contact.

What to prioritize
- Proper licensing and insurance: Florida contractor license (and local county requirements), current general liability and workers’ comp insurance. Get license numbers and verify them.
- Miami‑Dade and/or Florida Building Code compliance: look for contractors who install systems with Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) products or other manufacturer-approved, wind‑rated assemblies.
- Manufacturer certifications: e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc. These show training and access to extended warranties.
- Wind‑uplift and attachment details: contractors should specify fastening pattern, nail types, number of fasteners, use of hurricane clips or straps, and uplift ratings for the assembly.
- Experience with your roof type: steep asphalt shingle vs. tile vs. TPO/EPDM/PVC or modified bitumen for flats — hurricane techniques differ.
- Insurance-claim experience: if replacing via homeowner’s insurance, pick contractors experienced with adjusters and documentation.
- Warranties: manufacturer (material) warranty and a clear written workmanship warranty; get coverage details in writing.
- Reputation and references: recent project photos, local references, high ratings on Google/Angi/Yelp, and a solid BBB record (A+ or fewer complaints).

How to verify and check contractors
- Verify Florida license and status at the Florida Department of Business & Professional Regulation (search by license number).
- Ask for proof of insurance and call the carrier to confirm coverage and policy limits.
- Ask for NOA or product approval numbers for the proposed materials; verify on the Miami‑Dade County building code website.
- Check Google/Yelp/Angi and the BBB for reviews and complaint history.
- Ask for recent local references (same roof type and hurricane-rated system). Call them.

Questions to ask every contractor (use this checklist)
1. Provide Florida license number and proof of insurance. May I verify?
2. Are you experienced with Miami‑Dade NOA-approved systems? Which NOA numbers will you use?
3. What wind rating (mph) will the completed roof assembly meet?
4. Will you use hurricane clips/straps and how many fasteners per shingle/ply?
5. What exactly is included in the scope (decking, underlayment, drip edge, ice/water barrier, ventilation, flashing)?
6. Who will pull permits and handle inspections?
7. What manufacturer warranties and workmanship warranties are provided (length and coverage)?
8. Can you provide at least 3 recent local references and photos of completed jobs?
9. How do you handle disposal and permits, and will I get lien waivers?
10. What is the payment schedule and final inspection/cleanup plan?

Red flags
- No license or lapsed insurance
- High pressure for upfront large deposits (never pay full price up front)
- Vague scope or no written contract
- No local references or poor online reviews
- Refusal to pull permits or provide NOA/product approval info

Where to find contractors
- Local searches: Google Maps, Yelp, Angi and HomeAdvisor (read recent reviews).
- Miami‑Dade product approvals / contractor lists for NOA products.
- BBB for complaints and business profiles.
- Ask neighbors or HOA for contractors who have done hurricane upgrades.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated hurricane‑roof contractors near your ZIP code.
- Draft an email/template you can send to contractors to request bids and documentation.
Tell me your ZIP code or upload pictures/specs of your roof and I’ll produce a short vetted list and sample contact template.
